newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish T-bill yields seen unmoved by Sept CPI data.
newsitem.headline: Polish T-bill yields seen unmoved by Sept CPI data.

text.p: Polish T-bill secondary market yields were unmoved by uninspiring September CPI data, which at 1.9 percent growth topped market expectations, dealers said.

They said the September rise would likely delay a central bank interest rate cut until the first quarter of 1997, but T-bill yields were likely to hold steady due to the recent balance at the treasury's primary auctions.

"Primary auctions have been balanced recently, and this should not change on September's CPI data -- any growth of average yields should be capped at the present level of maximum yields," said Marek Wieczorkiewicz, chief dealer at PKO BP.
Poland's CPI fell to 19.5 percent in year-on-year terms from 20.5 percent in September. The finance ministry and the central bank forecast inflation to fall 19 percent last month.
"The ministry's and the central bank's forecasts did not materialise, which underlined that there is no room for a rate cut," said one analyst at foreign investment company here.
"With only cosmetic changes, T-bill yields should stay steady with benchmark 52-week paper around 19.40 percent," the analyst added.
On Tuesday the benchnmark bill was quoted at 19.45/42 percent against an average primary yield of 19.43 percent.
Overnight deposits were quoted at 17.8/18.3 percent against the opening at 17.9/18.1 percent. Tomorrow/next were at 17.9/18.4 percent versus opening's 18.00/18.15 percent.
The zloty closed weaker against the basket of currencies at 1.94/1.91 percent from the trading band centre from Monday's close at 1.98/1.96 percent from parity after a busy session.

Dealers said the zloty lost some ground against the bulish dollar and partly because of client based sell orders, which dominated active trade on Tuesday. It closed at 2.8220/30 per dollar, down from 2.8152/59 on Monday and at 1.8344/50 to the mark, up from 1.8390/96. -- Krzysztof Wojcik +48 22 653 9700
